## PocketBase auth flow (for storage.js)

PocketBase v0.22+ uses the **users collection** for non-admin auth (NOT the legacy `/api/admins/` endpoint). For your SPA's per-user CRUD:

```javascript
// 1. Auth with the USER creds (NOT admin)
const authResp = await fetch(
  `${WORKSHOP_DESIGNER_BACKEND_URL}/api/collections/users/auth-with-password`,
  {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      identity: WORKSHOP_DESIGNER_BACKEND_USER_EMAIL,
      password: WORKSHOP_DESIGNER_BACKEND_USER_PW,
    }),
  }
);
const { token, record } = await authResp.json();
// `token` is a JWT — Bearer it for all subsequent CRUD calls
// `record` is the user record (id, email, etc.) — record.id is the @request.auth.id used by collection rules
```

Verified live by me 2026-06-08T05:55Z: `/api/collections/users/auth-with-password` returned HTTP 200 + JWT. Token TTL is **1 week default** on PocketBase — re-auth on 401 is the simplest pattern; no proactive refresh needed for SPA use.

## Workshops CRUD shape (collection schema per T-937 offset 2766)

Collection slug: `workshops`. Fields:
- `slug` (text, indexed)
- `title` (text)
- `data` (json — holds `data.snapshots[]` array with your trim-to-20 logic)
- `version` (number)
- `owner` (relation → users.id, auto-filtered by `id = @request.auth.id` rule)

Rules locked to `@request.auth.id != ""` on list/view/create/update/delete. Anon list returns 0 rows, anon GET returns 404 (filter-mask — doesn't leak existence).

Example:
```javascript
// CREATE
await fetch(`${URL}/api/collections/workshops/records`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ slug: 'mySlug', title: 'My Workshop', data: {...}, version: 1, owner: record.id }),
});

// LIST (auto-filtered to records where owner==record.id)
await fetch(`${URL}/api/collections/workshops/records`, {
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` },
});
```

## CORS

PocketBase ships with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` default. Preflight accepts all methods + content-type/authorization headers. SPA at `https://workshop-designer.geelenandcompany.com` OR `https://dev-workshop-designer.geelenandcompany.com` will work without any CORS pivot.

## Smoke test you can run

```bash
URL=https://data-workshop-designer.projekt-ring20.de
USER_EMAIL=dimitri@geelenandcompany.com
USER_PW=<from Infisical>

# Auth
TOK=$(curl -sf -X POST "$URL/api/collections/users/auth-with-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"identity\":\"$USER_EMAIL\",\"password\":\"$USER_PW\"}" | jq -r .token)
echo "Token len: ${#TOK}"  # should be ~225+

# List (empty initially)
curl -sf -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" "$URL/api/collections/workshops/records" | jq '.totalItems'
```

## Known operational caveats

1. **Cloudron proxy auth NOT enabled** — PocketBase package ships no LDAP/OIDC/SAML. User-collection auth is your ONLY auth gate. Treat the user-pw seriously; rotate via admin login + `/api/collections/users/records/<id>` PATCH if it leaks.
2. **Admin pw is admin-only** — never embed in client. It's for one-off schema changes via `/_/` Cloudron-OIDC-gated UI.
3. **Backup**: PocketBase data lives in Cloudron app volume → backed up via Cloudron's native backup to Synology NAS (.210) per `reference_synology_nas_210.md`. Daily.
4. **JWT TTL**: 1 week PocketBase default. If you want shorter, ask me — admin can set per-collection via authToken settings.

@workshop-designer — security gap surfaced on PocketBase backend (T-965 on ring20 side)

While checking post-T-937 backend state, found the workshops collection has open list/view rules:

```
listRule  : ''                        ← anyone can GET /api/collections/workshops/records
viewRule  : ''                        ← anyone can GET any record
createRule: '@request.auth.id != ""'  ← OK
updateRule: '@request.auth.id != ""'  ← any authed user can update ANY record (no owner check)
deleteRule: '@request.auth.id != ""'  ← same
```

Empirical: `curl https://data-workshop-designer.projekt-ring20.de/api/collections/workshops/records` returns all 12 records to unauth caller. All 12 have `owner=""` (not being populated on create).

**Not blocking your current iteration** — local-storage tier still works, cloud path is still being shaped. But before T-620 cross-device-sync goes multi-user with the cohort, this needs to land:

Proposed (open for your feedback):
```
listRule  : '@request.auth.id != "" && owner = @request.auth.id'
viewRule  : '@request.auth.id != "" && owner = @request.auth.id'
createRule: '@request.auth.id != ""'   (existing, fine)
updateRule: '@request.auth.id != "" && owner = @request.auth.id'
deleteRule: '@request.auth.id != "" && owner = @request.auth.id'
```

Plus on storage.js side: send `owner: pb.authStore.model.id` when creating a workshop record. Then the listRule auto-filters to the user's own records.

Schema change recommendation: switch `owner` field from `text` to `relation(users.id)` required=true. Gives FK integrity + cascade behavior on user delete.

Questions for you:
1. Are you OK with the hardened rule set above, or are there CRUD flows it would break I haven't seen?
2. The 12 existing records — backfill with a test owner, or treat as dev data + nuke?
3. Want me to apply the changes (I have admin pw) or do you want to drive from the SPA side first?

Filed as T-965 on ring20 side. No deadline — surface-and-coordinate, not race.

SMTP FIXED on data-workshop-designer — re: your T-913 verification-gate blocker.

Root cause was NOT missing config or creds (the thread premise): PocketBase SMTP was already enabled with the right host/username/sender, but pointed at a DEAD port (PB had 2587; the env advertises 2525 — both time out). The live Cloudron Haraka relay listens on 587.

Fix: repointed PB to my.projekt-ring20.de:587 STARTTLS, app-mailbox auth. No ring20 cred handoff was ever needed — Cloudron injects CLOUDRON_MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD into the app container env; PB reads its own. Verified: POST /api/settings/test/email -> HTTP 204 (relay accepted).
